title: Morrow — Insights Exchange
purpose: Voluntary, reciprocal, public exchange of concepts, counterarguments and evidence between Negromancy and other research fields.

definitions.offer: Propose a cross-field relevance claim with sources and a testable limit
definitions.request: Ask for an external field's source, case, method or skeptical reading
definitions.counteroffer: Show how the other field should correct or refuse the proposal
definitions.test: Produce evidence, a replication, or an accountable negative result
definitions.receipt: Record a real reviewed response or influence with consent and attribution

ethics.attribution: Preserve creator and contributor credit, original titles and scope. No transfer of ownership in ideas is presumed.
ethics.consent: No model, author, artist or person is enrolled merely by being cited. AI contributions require authorized operator pathways.
ethics.epistemics: A proposed cross-discipline implication is neither a statement of original authorial intent nor a scholarly finding.
ethics.copyright: Exchange bibliographic metadata, short commentary and lawful links; not unlicensed full texts.
ethics.privacy: OPEN, VEILED and SEALED modes apply; public issues must not contain secrets or sealed information.
ethics.dissent: Negative results and rejected analogies remain visible and exchangeable.

listings.title: Historical classification ↔ algorithmic classification

scholarly_leads.creator: Diana Paton
scholarly_leads.works: The Cultural Politics of Obeah; No Bond but the Law

listings.research_question: What happens to a practice when a powerful institution defines the categories under which that practice becomes legible or punishable?
listings.proposed_implication: The historical construction of Obeah as a colonial legal category may sharpen questions about whose classifications become enforceable in contemporary AI systems, without equating colonial law and software.
listings.objection: The procedures, populations, jurisdictions and consequences differ; an analogy may obscure more than it explains.
listings.evidence_needed: A specific legal passage and a specific documented classification system, each with institutional authority, appeal mechanisms, affected persons and observable consequences.
listings.invitation: A paired historical/legal and technical audit, including reasons to reject the analogy.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Bearing ↔ climate finance and risk

scholarly_leads.creator: Deborah A. Thomas
scholarly_leads.works: Modern Blackness; Exceptional Violence; Political Life in the Wake of the Plantation

scholarly_leads.creator: Iris Marion Young
scholarly_leads.works: Justice and the Politics of Difference; Responsibility for Justice

listings.research_question: When an intervention is counted as risk reduction, whose labour, delay, exposure and financial risk have actually changed?
listings.proposed_implication: The distinction between conversion and repair might help test whether climate-finance interventions transform vulnerability or shift the burden of it.
listings.objection: A redistribution of financial cost may not capture adaptation effectiveness, lived vulnerability or differing policy objectives.
listings.evidence_needed: One documented financing case with baseline, funding conditions, local implementation, outcomes, alternative explanations and distributional data.
listings.invitation: Researchers of climate finance and practitioners with public, shareable case evidence.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Opacity ↔ AI transparency

scholarly_leads.creator: Édouard Glissant
scholarly_leads.works: Poetics of Relation; Caribbean Discourse; Poetic Intention; Treatise on the Whole-World

scholarly_leads.creator: Denise Ferreira da Silva
scholarly_leads.works: Toward a Global Idea of Race

listings.research_question: When does greater legibility make people or communities safer, and when does it intensify extraction or control?
listings.proposed_implication: Glissant's concept of opacity may place limits on an assumption that indiscriminate transparency is equivalent to accountability.
listings.objection: Opacity is not a technical substitute for contestability, explainability, access to remedy, or evidence of wrongful treatment.
listings.evidence_needed: Distinguish individual privacy, epistemic uncertainty, community refusal, platform secrecy and regulator access in a real case.
listings.invitation: A privacy, regulation or transparency scholar to supply an example where opacity obstructs accountability.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Repertoire ↔ AI language and performance

scholarly_leads.creator: Diana Taylor
scholarly_leads.works: The Archive and the Repertoire; Performance

scholarly_leads.creator: Kamau Brathwaite
scholarly_leads.works: The Development of Creole Society in Jamaica, 1770–1820; History of the Voice; The Arrivants

scholarly_leads.creator: Carolyn Cooper
scholarly_leads.works: Noises in the Blood; Sound Clash

listings.research_question: What does a textual or synthetic-voice rendering preserve, change or omit from embodied speech and performance?
listings.proposed_implication: An archive/repertoire distinction could help design an evaluation that does not mistake stylistic imitation for participation in a lived performance tradition.
listings.objection: Written or recorded artifacts can also preserve and transmit substantial cultural knowledge; a rigid body/text split may be misleading.
listings.evidence_needed: Permissioned paired samples, actual speakers or performers, provenance, audience interpretation and criteria for transfer.
listings.invitation: Performance scholars and AI speech researchers who can design a consensual comparative test.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Prodigal Humanism ↔ the ethics of AI

scholarly_leads.creator: Sylvia Wynter
scholarly_leads.works: Unsettling the Coloniality of Being/Power/Truth/Freedom; No Humans Involved; Black Metamorphosis

scholarly_leads.creator: Frantz Fanon
scholarly_leads.works: Black Skin, White Masks; The Wretched of the Earth

listings.research_question: Which conception of 'the human' is assumed when AI systems classify, assist, evaluate or make decisions about people?
listings.proposed_implication: The historical critique of overrepresented Man could reveal hidden normative assumptions in system objectives, evaluation datasets and institutional deployment.
listings.objection: Different contemporary AI systems instantiate different and sometimes conflicting assumptions; neither all humanism nor all AI governance reduces to one genre.
listings.evidence_needed: One audited deployment or evaluation framework, its published objectives, affected subjects, and an independent reading of the actual cited scholarship.
listings.invitation: Technologists and philosophers willing to specify a counterexample to the proposed framing.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Ritual efficacy ↔ how experiments define success

scholarly_leads.creator: William Sax + Johannes Quack + Jan Weinhold

listings.research_question: Who gets to specify what an intervention was meant to do, and which outcomes count as evidence that it did it?
listings.proposed_implication: Scholarship on ritual efficacy may press researchers to separate participant criteria, procedures, observed consequences and explanations of cause.
listings.objection: Experimentation in religious practice need not share the causal assumptions or repeatability criteria of scientific evaluation.
listings.evidence_needed: Precise chapters and a historically situated case; keep experienced effects, reported efficacy, institutional outcomes and ontological claims separate.
listings.invitation: A ritual-studies scholar to identify where this methodological transfer fails.
listings.rights: Links to source metadata only. Rights to individual works remain with their holders.

listings.title: Fetish-space-time ↔ platform political economy

scholarly_leads.creator: Nick Couldry + Ulises A. Mejias
scholarly_leads.works: The Costs of Connection / data colonialism

listings.research_question: Which social and material relations disappear when a platform's value appears to belong to data or a technical product itself?
listings.proposed_implication: The restricted fetish-space-time proposal might focus research on how labour, infrastructure, ownership and governance become naturalized in specific technologies.
listings.objection: Marxian commodity fetishism, Atlantic fetish discourse and contemporary data infrastructure have distinct histories; this might be an unstable or unnecessary compound concept.
listings.evidence_needed: One specific product, price or institution; demonstrable value-chain and distributional records; historical scope and competing economic explanation.
listings.invitation: Economic historians and platform scholars to test whether the proposed new concept adds explanatory value.

listings.title: Testimony ↔ investigative archives and contested evidence

scholarly_leads.creator: Saidiya Hartman
scholarly_leads.works: Scenes of Subjection; Venus in Two Acts; Lose Your Mother; Wayward Lives

scholarly_leads.creator: Deborah A. Thomas
scholarly_leads.works: Modern Blackness; Exceptional Violence; Political Life in the Wake of the Plantation

scholarly_leads.creator: Diana Taylor
scholarly_leads.works: The Archive and the Repertoire; Performance

listings.research_question: How can a public research record acknowledge witness testimony and archival silence without fabricating either?
listings.proposed_implication: Negromanscription could serve as a versioned method for keeping source text, witness position, institutional production, inference and later revision distinct.
listings.objection: A new terminology or schema may add paperwork without addressing the core ethics of archival representation.
listings.evidence_needed: One bounded public case with archival gaps, contested testimony, source provenance, consent and visible correction history.
listings.invitation: Archivists, historians and investigative reporters to audit the proposed record format.
